headline: Dynamical criticality and attractor dynamics as candidate brain connectivity markers
label: Brain Connectivity Biomarkers
summary: Directed, network-level dynamics are being quantified as candidate markers across human MEG, mouse fMRI modeling, and rodent EEG decoding.
synthesis: The dominant thread is a shift from static pairwise connectivity toward dynamical, network-level properties of neural activity. Resting-state human MEG shows power-law scaling and avalanche invariance under RG-inspired coarse-graining, with exponents linked to the analysis. A directed whole-cortex mouse network model, built on Allen-atlas connectivity, reproduces fMRI co-activation patterns through attractor dynamics. The EEG preprint departs from this framing: an asynchronous RNN decodes self-paced rat locomotion speed (r=0.88) from 32 skull electrodes, decoding behavior rather than mapping connectivity. What is new is the explicit treatment of these properties as candidate markers, each derived within a different modality and analysis framework rather than a shared pipeline.
